Ensemble. Five cross-validation folds × two seeds. Each network is fine-tuned on a different 80% of the 3,484 expert-labelled CrohnIPI frames, and the app averages all ten.
Severity. Class probabilities are summed inside each tier (none, mild, moderate, severe). That makes the grade ordinal, which is why it is scored with weighted kappa.
Explainability. Class-activation maps come out of the ONNX graph, so the heat-map costs nothing extra at inference.
Honest evaluation. Thresholds are chosen on other folds (cross-fitting), and recipes were fixed before scoring. External datasets were touched only once the model was final.
Deployment. FastAPI serves the ONNX models with onnxruntime on CPU, and a pre-built Next.js site is the UI. There is no PyTorch at runtime.

An LLM Supervisor classifies every message into one of four routes:
db — DBAgent — Natural-language SQL over company.db / MySQL
tool — ToolAgent — Email with Draft → Confirm → Execute HitL
Every agent output passes through a Validation Agent that re-grounds and normalises the answer into {answer, source, confidence} before returning to the caller.
Grader: LLM scores each retrieved document as relevant/irrelevant; fail-opens on error.
Rewriter: rewrites the query to be more search-friendly before retrying.
Child chunks — 200 tokens — Stored in Qdrant — precise semantic retrieval
Parent chunks — 800 tokens — Stored in ParentStore (JSON) — richer LLM context
After reranking, each retrieved child is swapped for its parent text before being passed to the answer LLM.
CompanyRetriever runs a 5-stage pipeline on every query:
Query rewrite — LLM expands the query (acronyms, keywords)
Dense search — Qdrant similaritysearch (top retrievertopk × 4)
Sparse search — BM25 over the same corpus
CrossEncoder rerank — cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 scores all candidates; top retrievertopk kept
Parent expansion — child chunks replaced with their 800-token parents
Two-tier auth: X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer — requireidentity for /chat, requireadmin for /settings, /upload, /documents
Prompt injection guard: 8-pattern substring check at the /chat boundary
SQL lockdown: read-only SQLite URI (mode=ro), usersettings table hidden from the SQL agent
Upload sanitisation: os.path.basename, extension allow-list, 20 MB size cap
Email guardrails: domain allow-list, hourly send cap, Draft → Confirm → Execute protocol
Secret masking: /settings GET returns "set" — never decrypts to caller
Rate limiting: Redis INCR keyed on source IP, 10 req/min default
Semantic cache: Qdrant ANN lookup; cosine similarity ≥ 0.96 skips the full pipeline
Redis-backed indexing queue: INDEXINGQUEUE is a Redis set (orchestrator:indexingqueue) — safe across multiple workers
Qdrant lock safety: retriever releases the file lock (client.close()) before background re-indexing runs
Pooled Redis client: single connection reused across rate-limit and queue helpers

points.t: Deep DCGAN Reproducibility Study Architecture & Analytics
points.s: A research-centric implementation of the DCGAN paper (Radford et al., 2015), modernized with 2018-2022 stability techniques and a professional post-training analytics pipeline.
This project isn't just about training another GAN—it's about understanding it. While most implementations just show you a grid of fuzzy images, this study dives deep into the "black box"…
Modern Stability: Upgraded the 2015 baseline with LSGAN (Least Squares) and Spectral Normalization to prevent the dreaded "vanishing gradient" problem.
Deep Diagnostics: A custom GANAnalyzer class that hooks into the model's internal layers to visualize learned filters and feature maps without needing to retrain.
High-Fidelity Evaluation: Automated 4-panel dashboarding for immediate assessments of model convergence and Nash Equilibrium.

points.t: DCGAN Reproducibility Study Paper vs. Modern Implementation
points.s: A formal comparison between the baseline architecture proposed by Radford et al. (2015) and this enhanced, high-stability version for facial/object generation.
While this project replicates the All-Convolutional architecture and upsampling strategy defined in the 2015 paper, it adopts several modern training paradigms discovered between 2017 and…
Loss Function — Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) — Least Squares GAN (LSGAN) — BCE suffers from vanishing gradients when the D is too strong. LSGAN (Mean Squared Error) forces the G to generate…
D Normalization — Batch Normalization — Spectral Normalization — Spectral Norm enforces a Lipschitz constant of 1, providing a mathematical guarantee against the Discriminator's gradients…
Weight Init — Normal(0, 0.02) — Modern Xavier/Kaiming Hybrid — Faster convergence and better flow of gradients through deep strided convolutions.
Regularization — None — D-Dropout (0.3) — Prevents the Discriminator from "overfitting" on the real dataset, which often causes the Generator to fail mid-training.
Labels — Hard Labels [0, 1] — Label Smoothing [0.1, 0.9] — Softens the target for the Discriminator to prevent it from becoming "too confident," which helps maintain gradient flow for the…

Confidence Histograms: Plot $D(x)$ vs $D(G(z))$ score distributions to see exactly how well the model separates real from fake.
